chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who catches a thief: is it better to let him go, or to bring him forward? He said: “Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah was reclining in the mosque upon his cloak. Then he got up to urinate, and when he returned it had been taken. So he searched for the one responsible and found him, then brought him to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he said: ‘Cut off his hand.’”
Ṣafwān said: “O Messenger of Allah, I gift that to him.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Why was that not before you brought him to me?”
He said: And I asked him about pardoning prescribed punishments before the matter reaches the Imam, and he said: “It is good.”

key_terms.اللِّصَّ: the thief who is apprehended for stealing
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the authoritative ruler/judge to whom the case is brought
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: the prescribed legal punishments in sacred law
key_terms.الْعَفْوِ: pardoning or remitting the offense before formal adjudication
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, where the incident took place
key_terms.اِقْطَعُوا يَدَهُ: the command to carry out the hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.رِدَائِهِ: his cloak or outer garment that was stolen
key_terms.يَرْفَعُهُ: to bring the case before the authority

ai.seo_question: Can a theft victim pardon the thief before the case reaches the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on dealing with theft and the distinction between private pardon and a case that has already been brought before authority. It shows that remission is acceptable before the case reaches the Imam, but once formally submitted, the legal process proceeds. The report also preserves a Prophetic precedent involving Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah and theft in the mosque.
